newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-MANCINI SAYS FAREWELL TO SAMPDORIA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MANCINI SAYS FAREWELL TO SAMPDORIA.

text.p: Sampdoria striker Roberto Mancini announced on Friday that he would play his last game for the Genoa club at the weekend after 424 appearances.

The 32-year-old former Italy international has scored more goals in his career than any other player active in serie A -- 142 in total -- and has been a stalwart and crowd idol at Sampdoria for 15 seasons.
Mancini did not say where he would be playing next season although expectations are that it will be Lazio.
"I just want to announce that Sunday will be my last match in the blue hooped shirt," he told a news conference at a hotel outside Genoa where Sampdoria regularly gather before their league matches.
"I have been fortunate to play for a team that has given me so much, even more than I have given.

"I thank the fans, above all the fans, because I don't think there is a player better loved than me. It has been and is a great honour. They loved me from the start, even when I was playing hardly at all and not well," he said.

The departure of Mancini, who with Gianluca Vialli made up the "terrible twins" that helped Sampdoria win their first ever league title in 1990-91, had been widely expected but marked a final break with a glorious era at the club.

With his close friend Vialli, who left Sampdoria for Juventus in 1992, Mancini also won the European Cup Winners' Cup in 1991, the Italian Supercup the same year and three Italian Cups. He won a fourth Italian Cup in 1994.
The hugely talented but sometimes fiery Mancini was also voted the best player in serie A in 1988 and 1991.

Sampdoria have already signed German captain Juergen Klinsmann for next season while coach Sven-Goran Eriksson, with whom Mancini has a good relationship, is due to take over at Lazio and has been expected to take Mancini with him.
Mancini had been in talks with Inter earlier in the season but negotiations broke off in the face of outrage from Sampdoria fans who angrily protested.
"I have not signed any contract, we'll see," said Mancini when asked about his future. "Now I know that I am hurting people who wish me well. I hope one day to pay them back by returning as a coach."
Sampdoria, who have already clinched a UEFA Cup place next season, play Fiorentina in their final match.
"I don't know how I'll react," he said of Sunday's game. "Samp has been everything for me and my love for this shirt will never die."
